abstract-evidence.abstract: Operando neutron diffraction (ND) serves as a powerful tool for probing crystallographic sites of light elements such as lithium and oxygen in the structural lattice during charge and discharge cycles. However, its limited temporal resolution currently restricts real-time monitoring under high-rate conditions. To address this challenge, a flexible machine learning framework, termed the electrochemical to crystallographic parameter inference framework (ECPIF), is proposed. Using a LiNi0.8Co0.15Al0.05O2 (NCA)||graphite full cell as a model system, operando ND data are collected at rates of 0.2, 0.5, and 1 C. With electrochemical data employed as input features and crystallographic parameters as target outputs, the model trained on the 0.2 and 0.5 C datasets demonstrates excellent predictive performance on the 1 C validation set and successfully extrapolates to 2 C electrochemical data. This study introduces a general framework for directly and rapidly mapping electrochemical signals to crystallographic parameters, thereby enabling the rational design of high-performance battery materials.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is pivotal for the safe and economical operation of electric vehicles and stationary energy storage systems. However, the rapid expansion of machine-learning and hybrid prognostic models has fragmented evaluation practices and weakened the reliability of cross-study comparisons. This work provides a structured review of data-driven RUL prediction through a unified taxonomy linking each model family to its learning target, inductive assumptions, data requirements, and common failure modes. Methodologically, this review conducts a systematic literature mapping and fine-grained bibliographic tagging of 996 publications, with emphasis on the 2017–2025 period, and quantitatively analyzes research trends, dataset usage, validation protocols, and reporting conventions to clarify where performance claims are comparable. This work further summarizes the outstanding challenges at the data, methodological, and application levels, including dataset limitations and inconsistent end-of-life definitions, generalization and benchmarking fragmentation with insufficient uncertainty calibration, and deployment, safety, and standardization constraints.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is fundamental to safety assurance, lifecycle management, and rational resource utilization. Over the past four decades, battery lifetime prediction has undergone a structural methodological evolution. This review reveals a transition from equation-centric degradation modeling toward representation-driven and transferable learning frameworks. Early studies relied on handcrafted electrochemical descriptors and statistical pattern recognition for qualitative screening. The subsequent shift to quantitative prediction established three foundational equation-based paradigms: empirical cycle-capacity extrapolation, discharge-event damage accumulation under dynamic duty cycles, and electrochemical-parameter-based simulations grounded in transport processes and side-reaction kinetics. Although physically interpretable, these approaches were largely static and constrained by parameter identifiability and stress-dependent variability. Later developments integrated Bayesian filtering and data-driven learning to reformulate degradation prediction as an adaptive state-estimation problem with uncertainty quantification. More recent advances emphasize representation learning, where high-dimensional electrochemical signals are transformed into transferable degradation features, and cross-domain transfer mechanisms mitigate data scarcity and distribution shifts across heterogeneous cells and operating conditions. We argue that the central challenge has shifted from deriving explicit degradation equations to constructing robust degradation representations that remain consistent with electrochemical principles while generalizing across conditions. Future progress will depend on field-grounded fleet-scale representation learning, physics-informed frameworks that reconcile mechanistic fidelity with data efficiency, adaptive and privacy-preserving transfer under distribution shift, and trustworthy deployment enabled by calibrated uncertainty, active learning, and mechanism-consistent explainability.

abstract-evidence.abstract: The performance of phase change materials (PCMs) in thermal energy storage and thermal management systems is directly determined by their thermal properties. Targeted development of high-performance PCMs is underpinned by accurate elucidation of heat transport and phase change regulatory mechanisms, as well as efficient high-precision thermal property acquisition. Quantitative prediction of PCMs thermal properties, microscopic mechanism elucidation, multi-component screening cost reduction, and extreme-condition property characterization can be achieved via molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML). However, classical MD is limited by empirical potential accuracy and system adaptability, with insufficient prediction precision in complex multi-component PCMs, failing to balance first-principles-level accuracy and large-scale long-time simulation, thus restricting its application in high-performance PCM design. To address this bottleneck, machine learning potentials (MLPs) built from density functional theory (DFT)-accuracy datasets enable high-precision MD simulations combining first-principles-level accuracy and large-scale capability, resolving otherwise inaccessible microscopic mechanisms and enabling efficient calculation for multi-component systems intractable to classical MD. This integrated MD-ML route has attracted extensive research attention recently. Herein, state-of-the-art advances in MD, ML, and their deeply integrated methods for PCM thermal property research are systematically reviewed, with focus on balancing computational accuracy and efficiency via synergistic optimization. First, MD-based thermal property prediction is summarized, and atomic-scale regulatory mechanisms of interfacial thermal resistance, confinement effects, and microstructure on heat transport and phase change in composite PCMs are elucidated. Next, ML applications in this field are reviewed, and advantages, limitations, and applicable scenarios of different ML models across PCM systems are compared from core dimensions of prediction accuracy, generalization ability, and computational cost. Subsequently, MLP simulations are comprehensively discussed, with their core advantage highlighted: combining first-principles-level accuracy and large-scale long-time simulation capability to resolve otherwise inaccessible microscopic mechanisms, along with key challenges in transferability and multi-element system adaptability. Finally, after benchmarking of mainstream prediction methods, core technical challenges, improvement strategies, and future directions for MD- and ML-based thermal property prediction are identified. For future work, priority should be given to developing general MLPs for complex PCM systems and extreme conditions, building physically interpretable ML models and standardized thermal datasets, closing the ML-MD simulation-experiment validation loop, and realizing high-throughput screening and inverse design of target PCMs.

abstract-evidence.abstract: The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is the core half-reaction of water electrolysis for hydrogen production, with hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔGH) as its key activity evaluation index. MXene, a new type of two-dimensional layered transition metal carbides, nitrides or carbonitrides, has great HER electrocatalytic potential due to adjustable electronic structure and geometric configuration. To solve the bottleneck that traditional “black box” models cannot provide interpretable guidance, this study constructed a dataset of 1125 MXene configurations, used XGBoost model to predict ΔGH (training set R2 = 0.953, MAE = 0.210 eV; test set R2 = 0.827, MAE = 0.390 eV). Finally, high-activity MXenes’ key structural boundary (GT-17 = 0, IET ≥ 10) is clarified, and O/S-functionalized MXenes are more likely to achieve optimal ΔGH close to 0 eV, providing guidance for rational design.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurate prediction of battery capacity aging trajectories is critical for reliable battery management, yet remains challenging due to complex electrochemical degradation mechanisms. While emerging time-series large language models (LLMs) have shown promise, they often lack adherence to physical laws, resulting in inconsistent long-term forecasts. To bridge this gap, we propose a physics-informed time-series LLM (PiT-LLM). Specifically, PiT-LLM incorporates the Transformer backbone (T-backbone), a patch-based Transformer architecture with implicit physical dynamics designed to tokenize long historical sequences and extract global degradation patterns. This data-driven stream is coupled with the Pi-Learner, a sine-activated multi-layer perceptron physics branch that imposes three soft trajectory-shape priors on the predicted aging curve—monotonic non-increase, bounded curvature, and derivative consistency. Rather than embedding mechanism-specific governing equations, the Pi-Learner regularizes the prediction toward smooth, physically plausible state of health (SOH) trajectories that remain consistent with macroscopic battery aging behavior. Extensive experiments on heterogeneous in-domain and external zero-shot datasets spanning NMC, LCO, LFP, and NCA chemistries show that PiT-LLM provides a strong accuracy-stability trade-off across both in-domain and cross-chemistry settings. Across the in-domain benchmarks, PiT-LLM ranks first on 6 of 9 MAE cells and 5 of 9 RMSE cells, while on the SNL zero-shot test, it remains within the top three on all six MAE/RMSE-horizon axes. These results demonstrate that trajectory-level physical priors strengthen time-series LLMs for long-horizon, cross-chemistry battery health prognosis.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Quantifying LiF in the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is critical for developing novel interface engineering and understanding battery degradation. However, conventional techniques (XPS, FTIR) face severe limitations in quantifying LiF due to shallow detection depth or low sensitivity. Far‑infrared (FIR) spectroscopy offers a potential advantage via the characteristic lattice absorption of LiF, yet its application is hindered by broad, strongly overlapping peaks and the lack of reliable concentration labels in real SEI samples. To overcome these challenges, inspired by the phenomenon that metastable SEI components can be transformed into stable products in a high-humidity atmosphere, this work constructs a simplified simulated SEI mixture and systematically collects its FIR spectra. A novel one‑dimensional convolutional neural network, AMDG‑1D CNN, is developed for LiF quantification, integrating adaptive preprocessing, multi‑scale feature extraction, dual attention refinement, and global multi‑statistics pooling. The model achieves a test R2 of 0.904 and RMSE of 3.706 wt%, outperforming conventional methods. It also shows strong robustness under various interferences. When applied to real SEI samples, predicted LiF concentrations show small deviations from ion chromatography measurements, validating the transferability from simulated to practical systems. This FIR‑deep learning framework provides a reference strategy for LiF quantification in complex electrochemical interfaces.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Fast-charging accelerates lithium-ion battery aging through complex, coupled physicochemical mechanisms that remain obscured in conventional data-driven state-of-health (SOH) models. To address this interpretability gap, we develop a prior-informed and interpretable workflow that combines the constant voltage (CV) stage current-feature extraction, physics-weighted principal component analysis (PW-PCA), XGBoost regression, and model-attribution analysis. Eighteen CV-stage current features were extracted from twelve LiNixCoyMnzO2 (NCM)//graphite 18650 cells cycled under six charge-discharge protocols at 45 °C. PW-PCA transformed the screened current features into three candidate latent descriptors, among which PC1 and PC3 were selected by PC-level ablation as the final predictive inputs. The resulting XGBoost model achieved accurate held-out SOH prediction with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0278 and an R2 of 0.864. SHapley additive explanations (SHAP) and XGBoost intrinsic importance consistently identified PC1 as the dominant descriptor, while PC3 provided complementary predictive information. Attribution analysis across aging stages and protocols further revealed protocol-dependent descriptor patterns under the tested accelerated-aging conditions. Among the six tested protocols, C3D2, denoting 3 C charging and 2 C discharging, showed the best observed trade-off among cycle life, capacity retention, and degradation rate. This work demonstrates a transparent workflow for connecting CV-stage current descriptors with interpretable SOH prediction and attribution-informed protocol screening within a controlled accelerated-aging dataset.

abstract-evidence.abstract: The electrochemical oxidative coupling of methane in solid oxide electrolysis cells offers a promising route for ethylene production, yet rational anode design remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a machine learning-accelerated discovery of efficient perovskite anodes for electrochemical oxidative coupling of methane. An ensemble model integrating four base learners identified the electronegativity and ionic radius of the B-site cation as critical descriptors, enabling the rational design of anodes that simultaneously fulfill the requirements of high oxygen evolution activity and effective CH4 activation. From 1019 candidates, several compositions were synthesized, among which SrCo0.9Ta0.1O3−δ exhibited exceptional performance, achieving a methane conversion rate to C2+ products of 600 μL min−1 cm−2 with 62% selectivity at 850 °C. This constitutes a substantial improvement over the commercial benchmark La0.6Sr0.4Co0.2Fe0.8O3−δ, which exhibited only 39% selectivity and a conversion rate of 330 μL min−1 cm−2 under identical conditions. Density functional theory calculations revealed that the predicted perovskite stabilizes reactive oxygen species (O22–) during the oxygen evolution reaction, thereby facilitating methane activation. This work presents a robust machine learning guided framework for rational design of multifunctional perovskite anodes that enable efficient methane conversion.

abstract-evidence.abstract: The escalating volume of literature demands automated knowledge extraction for autonomous robotic experimentation. This review traces the evolution from traditional rule-based and machine-learning pipelines to transformer-based large language models and multimodal architectures, encompassing domain-specific encoders and visual foundation models. We identify three persistent challenges: semantic complexity, multimodal heterogeneity, and rapid terminology evolution. We demonstrate that multimodal large language models, through context-aware reasoning, few-shot adaptation, and native cross-modal alignment, can systematically address these challenges, enabling holistic document-level understanding. Strategies including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning further enhance extraction reliability. ChemRobot systems can build structured actionable knowledge bases from unstructured texts, tables, and figures, closing the loop from literature to autonomous experimentation. We conclude with a roadmap for developing intelligent Literature Readers, emphasizing multimodal benchmarks, efficient architectures, uncertainty quantification, and human-machine collaboration.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Machine learning offers promising health management solutions for addressing the wave of battery retirement, facilitating their reuse to extend their second life. It is capable of efficiently accomplishing the three tasks of remaining capacity estimation, fast sorting, and second-life health diagnosis for a variety of retired batteries under different retirement conditions by utilizing fast measurement data or daily operation data as input. Here, we identify the challenges of performance differences of retired batteries compared to new batteries, introduce a general framework based on machine learning for the three health management tasks, analyze typical retired battery datasets, and summarize the health management challenges that may be encountered by machine learning. Subsequently, the application of machine learning to the three health management tasks is discussed in detail, as well as the solutions to address the three types of tasks in the face of challenges such as data scarcity and insufficient generalization capabilities. Finally, we provide an in-depth discussion of the key challenges in health management of retired batteries and present a forward-looking framework for future health management systems, with a particular focus on intelligent robotic solutions equipped with advanced artificial intelligence (AI) agents. This work provides a roadmap for safer and more economically viable battery reuse.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping research on perovskite solar cells (PSCs) and perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) by uncovering complex nonlinear relationships and navigating high-dimensional materials and device design spaces. Existing reviews, however, have predominantly focused on predictive machine learning (ML), with comparatively limited attention to large language models (LLMs), methodological robustness, and practical strategies for building generalizable AI workflows. Here, we review AI-driven advances from predictive ML to LLM-enabled knowledge extraction and reasoning, encompassing device performance optimization, fabrication optimization, mechanistic understanding, and automated experimentation. We critically examine three persistent challenges: model generalization under scarce and heterogeneous data, the distinction between statistical associations and causal physical mechanisms, and the integration of physical knowledge into data-driven models. We further assess the complementary roles of ML and LLMs: ML remains central to quantitative prediction and optimization, whereas LLMs support literature mining, knowledge synthesis, hypothesis generation, and experimental planning but require knowledge grounding and verification to mitigate hallucinations and physically implausible outputs. Finally, we outline a roadmap based on standardized metadata and community-wide benchmarks, uncertainty-aware and out-of-distribution evaluation, in situ diagnostics, physics-informed learning, and closed-loop experimentation. This framework aims to guide the development of trustworthy and transferable AI for perovskite optoelectronics.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Multi-contrast MRI super-resolution assisted by auxiliary anatomical guidance has emerged as a pivotal strategy for accelerating clinical imaging protocols. While diffusion models (DMs) demonstrate promising capabilities in this domain, two critical limitations hinder their diagnostic applicability: (1) insufficient utilization of high-frequency edge features across multi-contrast inputs, leading to anatomically inconsistent boundary construction, and (2) inflexible fusion mechanisms that fail to adequately model cross-modality dependencies, resulting in structural distortions. To address these challenges, we propose an edge-guided conditional diffusion model (i.e., Eg-Diff) for multi-contrast MRI super-resolution. To preserve high-frequency anatomical details, we design high-frequency-injected encoders in which contrast-adaptive edge features, captured by learnable detection operators, are exploited for hierarchical injection. Furthermore, to promote multi-modality synergy, adaptive multi-modality feature fusion is developed. Through contrast-weighted gating and K-selective balanced attention, it dynamically calibrates auxiliary guidance, enabling precise auxiliary prior utilization while suppressing modality bias. In the reverse diffusion process, to minimize noise interference, we propose a proactive activation strategy that discriminatively integrates the edge features as prior conditions for diffusion. Extensive experiments on IXI and MRBrainS13 datasets demonstrate that Eg-Diff outperforms state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its potential for clinical applications.

abstract-evidence.abstract: In line with the development of deep learning, this survey examines the transformative role of Transformers and foundation models in advancing visual anomaly detection (VAD). We explore how these architectures, with their global receptive fields and adaptability, address challenges such as long-range dependency modeling, contextual modeling and data scarcity. The survey categorizes VAD methods into reconstruction-based, feature-based and zero/few-shot approaches, highlighting the paradigm shift brought about by foundation models. By integrating attention mechanisms and leveraging large-scale pre-training, Transformers and foundation models enable more robust, interpretable, and scalable anomaly detection solutions. This work provides a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art techniques, their strengths, limitations, and emerging trends in leveraging these architectures for VAD.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well in general medical fields, but their effective application in complex liver disease diagnosis remains an open question. We propose an LLM-based Multi-agent Activated Graph-reasoning Intelligent Collaboration (MAGIC) model to address this challenge. MAGIC enhances liver disease knowledge through multi-scale analysis, including similar case studies, abnormal indicator identification, and knowledge graph analysis. During the simulated clinical progressive diagnostic process, the model adjusts key nodes and relationship weights in the graph reasoning using multi-agent debate results, improving pre-diagnosis accuracy. Meanwhile, the model verifies the pre-diagnosis results with guidelines to ensure their alignment with established clinical standards, ultimately generating reliable diagnostic results. Extensive experiments demonstrated that MAGIC achieved accuracy of 94.5 % on the dataset LiverQ&A from Beijing Friendship Hospital, 11.39 % improvement in F1 over the best LLM-based SOTA model. And MAGIC achieved 91.6 % accuracy on the multi-center validation dataset, which included data from Beijing You'an Hospital and China-Japan Friendship Hospital. Additionally, on the public dataset MedQA, our approach improved the accuracy of a closed-source model by 1.7 % to 6.8 %.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurate and automatic segmentation of brain gliomas is essential for early diagnosis and surgical planning. In recent years, the introduction of Transformers has facilitated the development of hybrid models combining CNN and Transformer in medical segmentation, leading to substantial performance improvements. However, most studies employ rigid fusion strategies, such as simple concatenation or weighted summation, to integrate local and global features. These approaches overlook differences in scale and semantics, resulting in insufficient feature interaction and fusion, which ultimately limits segmentation accuracy. To address this, we propose DDAFormer, a hybrid model that effectively integrates local and global features. The hybrid encoder includes a Large Kernel Cross-Modal Enhancement (LKCE) module to expand the receptive field and fuse cross-modal information, while the Distance-Aware Transformer (DAT) incorporates local features into global modeling, enhancing representation learning. In the decoding phase, the Dynamic Large Kernel Convolution (DLKC) module employs dynamic filtering to generate adaptive convolutional kernels, allowing the model to better capture the multi-scale and heterogeneous features of brain tumor images. This design enhances the integration of multi-scale information while improving the fusion of local details and global semantics. Additionally, we introduce a Multi-Scale Deep Supervision (MSD) Loss Function to optimize the decoder learning process, further enhancing segmentation stability. Experimental results on the BraTS2020, BraTS2021, and the MSD brain datasets demonstrate that DDAFormer outperforms state-of-the-art methods in segmentation accuracy, even with fewer parameters, highlighting its effectiveness and potential for medical image segmentation applications.

abstract-evidence.abstract: The scarcity of labeled multi-modal data is a key obstacle to sufficient multi-modal fusion. The traditional solution that uses ImageNet-pretrained weights as initialization usually results in biased learning due to the cross-domain/modal gaps. In this work, we overcome this limitation by proposing a self-supervised learning framework for multi-modal fusion. Unlike previous multi-modal contrastive learning architectures that are mainly performed by directly optimizing cross-modal agreement and always struggle with the information imbalance between modalities, especially for hard positive instances with noticeable modal-specific noises, we reformulate the multi-modal contrastive learning with imbalanced data to a unimodal contrastive problem to remove the modality gap. To this end, we combine the features from all modalities as a new modality representation. By performing contrastive learning on the synthetic modality, we facilitate pre-training for each modality and explicitly explore cross-modal correlation for downstream multi-modal fusion. To relieve the pre-training bias due to modality imbalance, we propose two strategies that selectively masking the discriminative features in the strong modality and reallocating the gradients more towards the weak modality to rebalance two modalities. Extensive experiments verify the effectiveness of our framework and designs on the downstream RGB-D salient object detection task and the generalization to RGB-T data.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Brain tumour is one of the most significant challenges in medical imaging, where early and accurate detection is crucial for improving patient outcomes. However, the lack of labelled Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) data severely limits the development of reliable diagnostic methods, resulting in issues such as class imbalance and reduced accuracy. This study addresses these challenges by leveraging Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate synthetic MRI images. We present a dual-enhancement pipeline with domain-specific innovations, combining contrastive SSL pretraining with GAN-augmented data to improve brain tumour classification. Our GAN architecture features medical-specific normalization layers, tumour-focused conditioning, and loss stabilization techniques to enhance the quality of synthesis. The SSL component employs domain-adapted, tumour-preserving augmentations and tailored pretext tasks (e.g., spatial context prediction) to ensure semantically meaningful representations. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showing an improvement in diagnostic precision. Additionally, the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) score indicates that the synthetic images exhibit a high degree of similarity to real MRI scans. These findings highlight the transformative potential of SSL techniques in mitigating the limitations associated with the lack of labelled medical data. Furthermore, the integration of Generative AI (GenAI) within multi-source (rather than multimodal) data fusion frameworks represents a significant advancement in medical imaging. By synthesizing and harmonizing diverse data sources, GenAI enhances information aggregation, which is particularly valuable in healthcare applications. Case studies and practical implementations demonstrate how GenAI-powered fusion methods enhance diagnostic accuracy; support improved patient monitoring, facilitate timely interventions, and enable more effective clinical decision-making. To support clinical integration, we incorporate explainable AI (XAI) methods to ensure transparency and interpretability, enabling rapid and informed decision-making in brain tumour detection. This research positions SSL and GenAI not merely as engineering tools but as essential enablers of data-efficient and precision-driven healthcare.

abstract-evidence.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel LLM-based KT model, called the Teacher Thinking Knowledge Tracing model (2T-KT), to solve the issue that traditional knowledge tracing methods relying on numerous student exercise records cannot make good predictions when predicting new knowledge concepts by leveraging the excellent abilities of reasoning and generation from large language model (LLM). The 2T-KT model leverages large language models (LLMs) to enrich the knowledge graph with new knowledge concepts and predict student performance on the next exercise by four key components, i.e. observation, guideline, interpretation, and cognition. In particular, there are two stages, the preprocessing stage, and the 2T-KT stage, to predict the student’s performance on the next exercise. In the preprocessing stage, two novel local and global knowledge graphs are first designed to improve the capability of evaluating new concepts. In the 2T-KT stage, a novel teacher’s thinking mode is designed to include four key components, i.e. observation, guideline, interpretation, and cognition to assist the LLM in predicting the student’s performance on the next exercise. This exercise contains new knowledge concepts. Finally, even with new concepts, the LLM ‘teacher’ can accurately predict students’ abilities through interpretable augmentation prompts. Extensive evaluations on three public educational benchmarks—the FrcSub dataset, comprising 10K student records and 8 exercises, and the Xes3g5m dataset, comprising around 522K student records and 6,641 exercises. In addition, the MOOCRadar dataset contains around 897K student records and 2510 exercise records to test our model’s performance. It demonstrates that our 2T-KT model is a strong contender in knowledge tracing, delivering both high performance and interpretability.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Monocular visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems are favored for compact automated devices owing to their cost efficiency. However, they face challenges with scale uncertainty due to restricted depth perception. Deep learning presents a viable solution to this dilemma, albeit with a trade-off: models that exhibit high accuracy are often too cumbersome for deployment on edge devices, while more compact models tend to sacrifice precision. In this paper, we introduce a light-weight monocular depth estimation network that employs the Transformer architecture, incorporating a novel encoder design that synergizes global and local perspectives alongside an initial feature fusion strategy within the decoder to enhance depth accuracy. Our approach outperforms existing methodologies in accuracy and model size across public datasets, significantly ameliorating localization errors in SLAM systems.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Foundation models hold great potential for medical image segmentation, but their application depends on extensive labeled data, the collection of which is often restricted by data privacy. In response, denoising diffusion probabilistic models have been used to synthesize realistic medical images for data augmentation. Meanwhile, federated learning enables distributed training and effectively safeguards data privacy. Nevertheless, existing approaches still face challenges regarding limited feature representation and insufficient adaptability to resource heterogeneity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unified approach that integrates the Highlight Diffusion Model (HDM) with semi-asynchronous federated learning (SAFedHDM). In this method, the HDM is trained locally on each client to generate highlighted features, thereby guiding the optimization of the segmentation model. On the server side, a parameter cache pool is introduced, along with version-aware strategies and a model drift synchronization mechanism, to enhance model consistency and training efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method improves the Dice coefficient by 1.5% to 3.2%, while also increasing communication efficiency to 1.67 to 5 times that of synchronous federated training, thereby providing a novel paradigm for federated foundation model training in medical image segmentation.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Omnidirectional image super-resolution (ODISR) is a critical technology for enhancing the quality of immersive visual experiences. Since equirectangular projection (ERP) is the commonly used storage format for omnidirectional images, existing ODISR methods leverage its geometric characteristics for super-resolution. However, they often ignore latitude-dependent self-similar features and prioritize optimizing average pixel distances, which tends to degrade visual quality. Moreover, the latent diffusion model (LDM) is often used to map images to a latent space during the diffusion process for efficiency. Yet, the designed autoencoder in the LDM for 2D images cannot adequately capture latitude-dependent characteristics, leading to misguided diffusion processes and degraded reconstruction quality. To alleviate these issues, we propose a new Latitude-Aware LDM (OSRLLDM), which fuses latitude information into the feature extraction process to obtain the high perceptual quality. Specifically, leveraging the latitude distortion characteristics of ERP images, we design the Vector Quantized Latitude-Aware Autoencoder (VQ-LAE). In VQ-LAE, deformable convolutions guided by latitude distortion maps adjust the receptive fields to learn geometric distortions caused by non-uniform pixel stretching. Meanwhile, the Latitude Self-Attention Block (LSAB) is introduced to capture spatial feature similarities within the same latitude, fully utilizing self-similar texture information to enhance the reconstruction quality. Additionally, to mitigate fidelity loss caused by the inherent randomness of diffusion models, the Pixel-Aware Control Block (PACB) is designed to guide the diffusion reconstruction process, achieving the balance between perceptual quality and fidelity. Experimental results demonstrate that OSRLLDM outperforms existing ODISR methods in objective perceptual metrics and subjective visual quality. The results and code will be made publicly accessible at https://github.com/liuleiming-GEM/OSRLLDM.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurately predicting pedestrian trajectories is crucial for the development of autonomous driving, robot navigation, and intelligent surveillance systems. However, this task remains extremely challenging due to the complexity of social interactions between pedestrians. Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been widely adopted in pedestrian trajectory prediction tasks due to their powerful interaction modeling capabilities and scalability. The GNN-based trajectory prediction methods construct different graph structures and then utilize graph convolution and its variants to capture pedestrian interaction features, thereby improving model prediction performance. To systematically review the research progress in this direction, this paper proposes a new classification method that divides the existing GNN-based methods into five types: conventional graph-based methods, sparse graph-based methods, multi-graph-based methods, heterogeneous graph-based methods, and higher-order graph-based methods. This paper systematically analyzes the modeling strategies, advantages, and disadvantages of each type of method to provide further guidance for subsequent researchers. In addition, we evaluate the prediction performance and inference time of these methods on public datasets and then discuss the current challenges and potential future directions of GNN-based trajectory prediction methods. A summary of related papers and codes is publicly available at https://github.com/Chenwangxing/Review-of-PTP-Based-on-GNNs.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurate ultrasound segmentation is crucial for intraoperative brain navigation and can improve non-rigid registration between preoperative MRI and intraoperative ultrasound, compensating for brain shift. However, limited annotated ultrasound data hinder the application of deep learning methods. Given recent advances in brain MRI-based medical image processing, transferring MRI datasets and deep learning models to US image research via cross-modal translation may potentially enhance intelligent brain US image processing. In this paper, we propose a novel cross-modality semi-supervised transfer learning from MRI to US by leveraging annotated data in the MRI modality. A diffusion model, leveraging conditional texture features and guided mutual information, transforms well-annotated MRI images into synthetic US images with a distribution closer to real US images. Subsequently, we employ a segmentation framework that involves pretraining with synthetic US images derived from MRI through image translation, followed by semi-supervised fine-tuning using a hybrid dataset that integrates both labeled and unlabeled ultrasound data. Extensive assessments are reported on the utility of SL-DDPM against competing GAN and diffusion models in MRI-US translation. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed transfer learning strategy achieves a segmentation accuracy of DSC of 93.43 ± 3.72 %. The effectiveness of our strategy is validated through ablation studies on fine-tuning strategies and semi-supervised learning, as well as comparisons with other state-of-the-art methods. Our transfer learning strategy enhances the accuracy and generalization of brain ultrasound segmentation models, even with limited hybrid training data, thereby assisting surgeons in identifying lesion.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Feature fusion is one of the keys to multimodal data segmentation. Different fusion mechanisms vary significantly in how effectively they utilize inter-modal features, exploit complementary information, and enhance representations, while also greatly affecting model parameters and computational complexity. Cross-attention fusion mechanism (CAFM) is the most widely used feature fusion mechanism in the current multimodal fusion classification task, but due to the inherent limitation, it cannot adapt to the differentiated feature requirements of different classes and leads to the blurring of interclass and dispersal features of intraclass. To address these challenges, a novel Category-Selective Feature Aggregation Transformer (CSFAFormer) is proposed to dynamically adjust the interaction weights between modalities along the class dimension, thereby fully leveraging the complementary advantages of different modalities. To accommodate the differentiated needs of different categories, a Category Cross-Calibration Mechanism (C3M) is designed to compress multi-channel features, estimate pixel-level class distributions, and employ a confidence-based cross-calibration strategy to dynamically adjust interaction weights along the class dimension, better accommodating the varying demands of different classes. To further semantic consistency and inter-class separability, a Category-Selective Transformer Module is proposed to leverage the class information calibrated by C3M for adaptive weighted fusion along the class dimension, thereby optimizing the representation of category-specific features. Experimental results indicate that CSFAFormer significantly outperforms in segmentation performance. Compared to the CAFM, CSFAFormer reduces the parameter count by 38.5 % and the computational cost by 72.3 %, while maintaining superior performance. The code is available at: https://github.com/NUAALISILab/CSFAFormer.

Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant promise for reasoning problems. They are among the leading techniques for context inference, particularly in scenarios with strong sequential dependencies, where earlier inputs dynamically influence subsequent responses. However, existing reasoning paradigms such as X-of-thoughts (XoT) typically rely on unidirectional, left-to-right inference with limited inference paths. This renders them ineffective in handling inherent skip logic and multi-path reasoning, especially for contexts such as a multi-turn social survey. To address this, we propose Random Forest of Thoughts (RFoT), a novel prompting framework grounded in the principles of reasoning path fusion for skip logic. It uses Iterative Chain-of-Thought (ICoT) prompting to generate a diverse set of reasoning thoughts. These thoughts are then assessed using a cooperative contribution evaluator to estimate their contribution. By randomly sampling and fusing the top-
𝑘
 reasoning thoughts, RFoT simulates uncertain skip logic and constructs a rich forest of plausible thoughts. This enables it to achieve robust multi-path reasoning, where each question sequence formed by the skip logic is treated as an independent reasoning path. RFoT is validated on two classic social problems featuring strong skip logic, using three open-source LLMs and five datasets that have been categorized as structured social surveys and public social media data. Experimental results demonstrate that RFoT significantly enhances inference performance on problems that require complex, non-linear reasoning across both survey and social media data. The transparency and trustworthiness of the results stem from the interpretable fusion of diverse reasoning paths and the principled integration of cooperative evaluation mechanisms.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) have emerged and achieved good performance on numerous downstream tasks. However, different FMs, like CLIP, DINOv2, and SAM, are trained on diverse datasets with varying methodologies, exhibiting model-specific characteristics and encoding scenario-specific knowledge. Efforts to unify the strengths of these different FMs through knowledge distillation show promise but remain challenging due to the inconsistencies in feature distributions, which can lead to suboptimal convergence and reduced generalizability. In this paper, we propose a novel aggregation framework, FM2 (Fusing Multiple Foundation Models), which leverages disentangled representation learning to address these challenges. Specifically, our approach effectively disentangles consensus and divergence features from multiple expert FMs and then aligns them into a unified and robust representation. Extensive experiments on datasets with over 1,000,000 pathology images across various tasks, including zero-shot and few-shot classification, cross-modal retrieval, and survival analysis, demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models, delivering superior accuracy and reliability across various clinical scenarios. Additionally, the visualizations offer insights into the model’s ability to harmonize knowledge across different FMs, highlighting its potential for enhancing diagnostic precision in medical imaging. The significant advancements demonstrated in our work underscore the promise of effectively aligning FMs, showing potential for broadening their application not only in pathology but also in other medical imaging domains.

abstract-evidence.abstract: While opinions and actions are inherently coupled in group decision-making, existing studies often treat them separately—an impractical approach for emergency scenarios where agents must rapidly integrate personal and social cues to make safety-critical decisions. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel two-layer emergency decision-making framework with key innovations: (1) A reinforcement learning-based continuous opinion and discrete action (RLCODA) model at the decision layer, where agents dynamically optimize decisions through Q-learning to maximize cumulative rewards, enabling active and rapid adjustments; and (2) A behavioral motion rule that translates optimal decisions into directional movement. Unlike prior works, our framework quantitatively ensures faster convergence (verified by comparative experiments) while maintaining opinion-action-behavior coherence. Simulations on three real-world networks (Karate Club, Dolphin, Political Books) demonstrate two practical advances: (i) approximately 18 % faster evacuation completion than baseline models, and (ii) emergent polarization balancing during collective decision-making. The results validate RLCODA’s superiority in both decision efficiency (theoretical) and emergency responsiveness (applied), offering a paradigm shift for modeling real-time human collective behavior under pressure.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation provides precise descriptions of anatomical structures and pathological regions, which plays a crucial role in formulating effective treatment plans, guiding surgeries and monitoring disease progression. Recently, hybrid models combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transformers have been able to compensate for the limitations of traditional CNNs in capturing long-range dependencies. However, these models often exhibit insufficient generalization ability when confronted with unknown medical data. On the other hand, purely Transformer-based models, while possessing strong global modeling capabilities, face challenges of high computational complexity. To address these problems, this paper proposes a novel U-shaped pure Transformer architecture, called Dual Feature Aggregation Transformer (DFAFormer). A Dual Feature Aggregation Transformer Block (DFATB) is designed based on Feature Aggregation Feed-Forward Network (FAFN), which enhances the model’s ability to capture richer contextual information and complex features by integrating spatial aggregation attention and channel aggregation attention mechanisms. The FAFN module introduces a gating mechanism to capture nonlinear spatial information and reduce channel redundancy, achieving efficient feature extraction while reducing the computational complexity of the model. Additionally, the Differential Transformer is innovatively incorporated, which focuses on key information and suppresses unnecessary noise through differential operations, improving the model’s robustness and generalization capabilities. Extensive comparison and ablation experiments are conducted on the Synapse, ISIC 2018 and WORD dataset, achieving average Dice scores of 83.60 %, 92.27 % and 87.78 % respectively. Experiments have shown that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods, reducing computational complexity while exhibiting strong generalization ability and promising application prospects. The code will be released via https://github.com/Sunflower-li369/DFAFormer.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Hydrological flow forecasting is critical for water resource management, disaster early warning, and ecological protection. However, centralized modeling approaches face persistent challenges with data heterogeneity, scarcity of extreme-event samples, and privacy constraints. This manuscript demonstrates a novel paradigm for fusing heterogeneous, distributed hydrological data while preserving privacy, creating a more robust and globally informed model than possible with isolated data silos. We propose Federated Learning Multi-Stations Fusion (FedMSF), which integrates local models with global aggregation to handle cross-basin variability without exposing raw data. A proximal term reduces training bias under distributional shifts, and a Multi-Objective Aggregation strategy (FedMOA) adaptively weights clients to enhance structural consistency. Additionally, extreme-aware data augmentation enriches the representation of rare events, while an AI-driven large language model (LLM) guides hyperparameter optimization. All reported metrics represent the mean performance across all catchments. Experiments on the CAMELS-GB West region show that FedMOA achieves RMSE of 0.4322, MAE of 0.2358, and NSE of 0.8371, outperforming existing methods by 7.93 %, 9.20 %, and 7.83 %, respectively. Furthermore, KGE improves by 4.48 % to 0.8127, while FLV and FHV decrease by 24.38 % and 34.7 %, respectively, indicating a reduction in volumetric errors. With the integration of augmentation and LLM-driven optimization, FedMSF further enhances performance, reaching an NSE of 0.8406, demonstrating improved robustness and generalization in cross-regional hydrological forecasting.

abstract-evidence.abstract: 3D semi-supervised semantic segmentation aims to mitigate heavy reliance on large-scale high-quality annotations to achieve accurate fine-grained and stereoscopic perception, and serves as a promising technique for intelligent industries. However, existing 3D semi-supervised methods primarily rely on single LiDAR-only representation or coupled multi-modal representation via unidirectional distillation, which typically overlook 2D semi-supervised learning, diminish modality-specific expression and underestimate image adaptability, and the powerful multi-modal potential for unlabeled data learning is still underexplored. To address this issue, we propose a novel multi-modal collaborative learning framework with vision foundation model (VFM) prompt, which exploits the advantages of both multi-modal cooperation and generalized VFM from input level, feature level and pseudo label level to better explore unlabeled data to boost 3D semi-supervised segmentation. Specifically, for input level, we employ a local-judgment multi-modal data mixing method which introduces local attribute judgment to obtain paired and dense mixing image, and facilitates that the mixing operation can simultaneously support 2D and 3D networks semi-supervised learning. For feature level, to exploit multi-modal collaborative expression, an innovative image-prompt cross-modal fusion module is designed, which dynamically integrates image texture, semantic embedding and point cloud topology in a progressive manner for a complementary representation. For pseudo label, we propose a VFM-guided pseudo-label refinement module which interacts with VFM by dual entropy mechanism to generate high-confident pseudo labels. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on three recognized 3D semantic segmentation datasets nuScenes, SemanticKITTI and ScribbleKITTI. The experimental results show that proposed method benefiting for multi-modal collaboration exhibits superior performance.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Microwave images with high spatiotemporal resolution are essential for observing and predicting tropical cyclones (TCs), including TC positioning, intensity estimation, and detection of concentric eyewall. Nevertheless, the temporal resolution of tropical cyclone microwave (TCMW) images is limited due to satellite quantity and orbit constraints, presenting a challenging problem for TC disaster forecasting. This research suggests a multi-sensor data fusion approach, using high-temporal-resolution tropical cyclone infrared (TCIR) images to generate synthetic TCMW images, offering a solution to this data scarcity problem. In particular, we introduce a deep learning network based on the Vision Transformer (TCA-ViT) to translate TCIR images into TCMW images. This can be viewed as a form of synthetic data generation, enhancing the available information for decision-making. We integrate a phase-based physical guidance mechanism into the training process. Furthermore, we have developed a dataset of TC infrared-to-microwave image conversions (TCIR2MW) for training and testing the model. Experimental results demonstrate the method’s capability in rapidly and accurately extracting key features of TCs. Leveraging techniques like Mask and Transfer Learning, it addresses the absence of TCMW images by generating MW images from IR images, thereby aiding downstream tasks like TC intensity and precipitation forecasting. This study introduces a novel approach to the field of TC image research, with the potential to advance deep learning in this direction and provide vital insights for real-time observation and prediction of global TCs. Our source code and data are publicly available online at https://github.com/kleenY/TCIR2MW.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Swin Transformer introduced window self-attention (WSA) to improve the performance of Vision Transformer (ViT) in semantic segmentation. However, the attention patch group partition in WSA is solely based on spatial positions, which ignores the spatial frequency relationships. It may limit the ability of attention mechanisms to fully exploit the inductive biases. To address this issue, we propose a novel attention mechanism that integrates traditional computer vision techniques with deep learning approaches, named Prior Information Attention (PIA). PIA redefines the grouping strategy by fusing edge prior information (edge detection results) to re-organize image patches into flexible group windows. It enables the attention computation to query image patches that share similar edge intensities but are spatially distant. Besides, Feature Exchanging Strategy (FES) is further introduced to refine feature boundaries via cross-group fusion. Building upon PIA and FES, we propose a transformer backbone named PIA Transformer (PIAT). To validate the effectiveness of PIAT, we compare it with the state-of-the-art semantic segmentation models on 4 datasets (Cityscapes, ADE20K, DLRSD and CamVid). Experimental results demonstrate that PIAT outperforms the baseline methods in all four datasets.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing images (RSIs) is challenged by the coexistence of coarse spatial layouts, fine structural boundaries, and heterogeneous textures that are distributed unevenly across frequency components. To better characterize these complementary properties, we introduce FSSFFormer, a frequency domain-enhanced transformer that leverages multi-resolution wavelet decomposition to enrich representation learning. A fixed 2D discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is first applied to decompose RSIs into low-frequency and high-frequency subbands, allowing the model to explicitly preserve global spatial structures while retaining fine-scale details. On top of these frequency-decomposed features, two lightweight modules are employed: a Spectral Enhancement Attention (SEA) module that selectively emphasizes informative subband responses, and a Spectral-Spatial Context Attention (SSCA) module that improves contextual modeling across the decomposed feature spectrum. The refined representation is subsequently reconstructed in the spatial domain using inverse DWT for dense prediction. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks, ISPRS Vaihingen, ISPRS Potsdam, and LoveDA, show that FSSFFormer delivers consistently strong performance, with notable gains in boundary fidelity as measured by BF-score. Ablation studies further demonstrate the complementary roles of subband decomposition and the two attention modules in enhancing both structural detail and semantic consistency.

abstract-evidence.abstract: In clinical practice, MRI commonly employs larger slice thickness and inter-slice spacing than CT, which predisposes to inter-slice gaps and potential loss of fine structural details and lesion boundary information. Moreover, CT acquisition is simple and fast, whereas MRI is time-consuming and requires patients to remain motionless; additionally, some patients cannot undergo MRI due to implanted metal devices. Therefore, achieving CT-guided generation of low–slice-thickness MRI images has become an important challenge. This study addresses the problem of CT-to-MRI cross-modal image translation in medical imaging by proposing a three-stage pipeline framework—DBT-DR-GAN—that integrates a dual-branch Transformer conditional GAN with a residual-predictive perceptual conditional diffusion denoising model to overcome the shortcomings of traditional methods in structural consistency and fine-texture recovery. First, data preprocessing is applied to effectively suppress background noise and extreme pixel outliers in the input images. Next, a novel dual-branch Transformer deep-residual conditional GAN is constructed to simultaneously capture global long-range dependencies and local detail features, achieving initial cross-modal synthesis. Finally, a residual-predictive perceptual conditional diffusion denoising model refines the preliminary outputs, further enhancing local detail and perceptual quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DBT-DR-GAN method significantly outperforms existing representative approaches in global structure preservation, soft-tissue texture recovery, and perceptual image quality, exhibiting promising potential for clinical application. This work offers new insights and methodologies for medical cross-modal image synthesis, and future studies may explore model generalization and lightweight designs to facilitate practical deployment.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD), a common form of dementia, is a progressive neurodegenerative condition that necessitates early and accurate diagnosis to minimize the risk of misdiagnosis, treatment delays, or inappropriate interventions as it advances from the cognitively normal (CN) stage to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and ultimately to AD. Interpreting diverse multimodal data for reliable diagnosis and progression monitoring typically depends on expert evaluation, which can be subjective. Moreover, existing automated methods often rely on rigid, discrete classifications that fail to account for uncertainty and transitional dynamics between stages. To address these limitations, the proposed method provides a comprehensive and structured input from multimodal data to generate a synthetic medical report as a supportive document with AI tool guidance in the absence of detailed analysis and handwritten reports. MRI and PET data are used to extract radiomic features and generate correlation maps at both whole-brain and sub-brain levels. This allows for the simultaneous assessment of structural atrophy and metabolic changes. Diagnostic classification into CN, MCI, and AD is performed using multiple machine learning models, with explicit identification of possible inter-stage and cross-modality conflicts. Additionally, principal component analysis (PCA) is applied to these correlation maps to detect longitudinal progression patterns, ranging from stable to aggressive trajectories, and to pinpoint the most affected brain regions. The resulting system not only enhances stage classification accuracy but also provides insight into disease evolution by leveraging the structural and functional relationships captured through radiomic correlations. These outputs, encompassing diagnostic insights, imaging-based findings, cognitive score trajectories, and conflict analysis, are structured into input data suitable for AI-guided synthetic ground-truth report generation due to the absence of handwritten data. The collection of the structured input and ground truth reports is used to fine-tune LLMs to obtain optimal and meaningful results. This approach enables the automatic production of detailed, personalized diagnostic reports. Ultimately, the integration of radiomic correlation mapping with PCA-driven progression analysis offers a robust, non-invasive, and automated decision-support tool for comprehensive AD evaluation and reporting.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Graph anomaly detection is crucial for identifying malicious activities in complex systems, such as financial fraud and network intrusions. When such sensitive data is distributed across multiple institutions with strict privacy constraints, Federated Graph Anomaly Detection (FGAD) becomes essential. However, FGAD is hindered by two fundamental challenges. First, graph partitioning severs cross-client edges, creating incomplete local views and biased representations. Second, existing methods rely heavily on generating pseudo-anomaly labels, a strategy that introduces significant label noise and fails to capture the global data distribution. To address these limitations, we propose FedDCL, a novel framework that pivots from relying on noisy pseudo-labels to implicitly learning the global distribution of normal patterns. At its core, FedDCL employs a Federated Conditional Diffusion Model (FedCDM) to construct a robust, global normality manifold from distributed subgraph embeddings. This approach successfully bypasses pseudo-label noise and aggregates a global view to prevent local overfitting. For inference, we introduce a streamlined Restoration-Consistency scoring mechanism that accurately identifies anomalies based on the incongruity between a node’s diffusion-restored normal representation and its original local context. Extensive experiments on multiple FGAD benchmark datasets demonstrate that FedDCL significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code is available at https://github.com/weihus/FedDCL.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Industrial time-series (ITS) anomaly detection is pivotal for ensuring the safety, reliability, and operational stability of complex industrial systems. Traditional centralized machine learning-based methods for ITS anomaly detection have gradually revealed issues such as difficulty in adapting to distributed data storage, meeting stringent privacy protection requirements, and achieving cross-institutional collaborative modeling, which limit their application and promotion. As a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, federated learning (FL) enables collaborative modeling among multiple participants without sharing raw local data, which offers a novel solution for ITS anomaly detection. However, the current application of FL for ITS anomaly detection remains in its preliminary exploratory stage and lacks a comprehensive synthesis. Therefore, this paper provides a systematic review of the research progress in FL for ITS anomaly detection, covering fundamental concepts, mainstream approaches, core challenges, and future directions. The limitations and advantages of FL-based ITS anomaly detection approaches are discussed and analyzed, and the core challenges faced by these approaches are summarized. Meanwhile, by integrating the practical requirements of ITS anomaly detection and technological development trends, several promising research directions are presented. This review aims to provide a systematic reference for deepening theoretical understanding and engineering application of FL for ITS anomaly detection.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies jointly capture gene expression profiles and spatial coordinates, providing new insights into tissue organization research. Existing clustering methods effectively exploit spot adjacency to identify domains exhibiting expression consistency and spatial continuity. Despite progress, these methods primarily model spatial adjacency while neglecting complementary gene dependencies and are further hindered by the high sparsity inherent in ST data. Here, we propose OrthoST, a transformer-based method that leverages dimension-orthogonal attention to jointly model spatial and gene dependencies for ST data analysis. By grouping spots into local contexts, OrthoST adapts non-sequential data to transformers and applies window spot attention and window gene attention to capture spatial and co-expression patterns. The model is trained by alternately reconstructing raw data and performing contrastive learning on views augmented by a plug-and-play extended bilateral filtering (EBF), thereby ensuring fidelity and reliable discriminability of embeddings. Extensive experiments across seven diverse ST datasets demonstrate that OrthoST achieves state-of-the-art performance in spatial domain identification, demonstrates strong robustness to dropout events, and effectively captures biologically meaningful gene relationships. These results establish OrthoST as a reliable and effective tool for accurate spatial domain identification, enabling understanding of tissue structure and function.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Incorporating brain structure-function interactions has been shown to enhance brain disorder diagnosis and cognitive prediction. However, current studies primarily focus on one-to-one interactions between corresponding regions of interest (ROIs), overlooking more complex interactions across different ROIs. Since ROIs within the same module exhibit more similar neural mechanisms of structure-function coupling compared to those in different modules, modular-level homogeneity provides stronger biological guidance for learning complex interactions. Though leveraging this guidance can further improve prediction performance, such studies remain scarce. To address this gap, we propose a modularity-guided attention-based graph neural network that extracts and emphasizes key structure-function interactions across ROIs relevant to specific tasks. Specifically, a modularity-guided interactive network is designed to define modularity-specific convolution operations learning interactions across structural and functional ROIs based on modular homogeneity. A modular interactive edge attention model is designed to highlight the most salient interactions by using a cross-attention mechanism. These identified interactions serve as edges connecting structural and functional ROIs, forming a unified graph. A graph transformer-based approach leverages this graph for prediction. Experimental results on three datasets demonstrate our model significantly outperforms nine state-of-the-art multi-modal methods in predicting fluid cognition, as well as in classifying Parkinson’s disease and schizophrenia. Attention maps show that the visual function engaging with default mode and frontoparietal structures is key to predicting fluid cognition, while diverse functional modules interacting with the subcortical structures are linked to Parkinson’s disease. Subcortical and visual-related structures interacting with the functional modules related to sensory and executive function are associated with schizophrenia.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Single hyperspectral image super-resolution aims to reconstruct the high-resolution counterpart of a hyperspectral scene from a single low-resolution input without external guidance. A major challenge lies in jointly modeling long-range spatial dependencies and complex spectral correlations under strict computational constraints. Standard Transformers suffer from quadratic complexity, making them impractical for high-dimensional data. Meanwhile, existing lightweight methods often exhibit limited receptive fields or decouple spatial-spectral modeling. To address these issues, we propose the Efficient Spatial-Spectral Transformer (ETNet). This architecture integrates global context modeling with local feature extraction. At its core is the Unified Spatial-Spectral Module (SSM), which captures global spatial context and inter-band correlations in a single block. We utilize the Spectral Correlation Coefficient (SCC) to guide affinity estimation, incorporating spectral priors into the attention mechanism. By adopting a kernelized formulation, ETNet achieves linear complexity while preserving a global receptive field. Furthermore, a channel attention submodule and a streamlined gated feed-forward network enhance representational efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ETNet achieves consistent gains over state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative performance and perceptual quality.

abstract-evidence.abstract: After natural disasters, rapidly and accurately detecting collapsed buildings is crucial for emergency rescue, post-disaster assessment, and reconstruction. However, existing point cloud-based detection methods for buildings have notable limitations: convolutional neural networks struggle to capture global structural relationships, Transformers exhibit quadratic computational complexity when processing large-scale point clouds, and Mamba lacks explicit global attention mechanisms. To address these issues, this paper proposes the CollTransMam network for collapsed building detection, which employs a hierarchical encoder-decoder architecture that innovatively combines the global attention advantage of Transformer with the linear complexity long-sequence modeling capability of Mamba. Specifically, the Fusion Conv module generates compact feature representations through efficient sampling, clustering, and feature fusion; the Grouping and Aggregation Block (GAB) module captures spatial correlations through multi-scale grouping and aggregation; the 3D Zigzag path converts unordered point clouds into ordered sequences; and the final Transformer-Mamba Fusion (TM-Fusion) module integrates the strengths of both Transformer and Mamba to achieve efficient global-local feature modeling. Experiments on two real earthquake disaster LiDAR point cloud datasets, KECB-PCD and PAPCB-PCD, show that the CollTransMam network significantly outperforms mainstream CNN, Transformer, and Mamba-based methods in core metrics such as accuracy, recall, IoU, OA, and mIoU. At the same time, the network has only 5.3M parameters and 5.4 FLOPs, with a computational complexity much lower than similar models, achieving a good balance between detection accuracy and efficiency, providing a reliable technical solution for rapid and accurate detection of collapsed buildings after disasters.

abstract-evidence.abstract: To address the critical role of Gut-Kidney Axis dysregulation in the progression of Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) and the challenge of effectively fusing spatial 3D kidney geometric data with non-Euclidean microbiome data, this paper proposes Point-BioGNN, a novel cross-domain Graph Neural Network framework. Employing a dual-stream architecture, the framework utilizes Dynamic Graph Convolutional Networks (DGCNN) to capture fine-grained morphological features from kidney point clouds and extracts high-order structural features of microbial communities via Graph Attention Networks (GAT). Leveraging a specialized Cross-Domain Attention Fusion module, the model achieves adaptive alignment of geometric and biological features in a latent space, effectively bridging the semantic gap between ”morphology and microecology.” Experiments on a clinical dataset demonstrate that Point-BioGNN significantly outperforms existing baseline models in disease prediction tasks. Furthermore, visualization analysis successfully uncovers deep associations between specific pathogenic genera and morphological changes in the renal cortex. This study not only validates the efficacy of multi-modal fusion but also provides an interpretable, non-invasive AI analytical tool for deciphering the interaction mechanisms of the Gut-Kidney Axis.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Multi-modal healthcare data challenges traditional machine learning models, causing misaligned features, overconfident predictions, and errors. Privacy concerns and dataset heterogeneity further limit AI scalability in healthcare. We propose a framework integrating multi-modal reasoning, hallucination mitigation, and uncertainty quantification. Our method uses Bayesian uncertainty quantification, cross-modal contrastive learning, and retrieval-augmented reasoning (RAR) to decrease hallucinations in large vision-language models (VLMs). We employ deep ensembles, Dirichlet-based calibration, and temperature scaling to improve the dependability of the model. Our system uses attention-driven fusion, dynamic modality weighting, and hierarchical interaction modeling to merge several modalities into a single representation through the Unified Multimodal Reasoning (UMR) Platform. It facilitates human-in-the-loop validation and temporal contextualization, which helps with adaptive learning and sound decision-making in dynamic clinical situations. We use rigorous assessment measures to show the efficacy of our approach. Innovative measuring criteria including the Clinical Consistency Score (CCS), Hallucination Rate Reduction (HRR), and Cross-Modal Alignment Index (CMAI) are employed. These metrics offer detailed information on how well the model performs in terms of clinical consistency, hallucination mitigation, and multi-modal alignment. Our framework exhibits notable enhancements when compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) models. Our models (LLaVA-Med + RAR, LLaVA-Med + CMCL, and LLaVA-Med + UMR) outperform the best-performing SOTA model (LLaVA-Med) by an average of 0.05 to 0.1 points across datasets in terms of BertScore. In terms of BLEU, our approach generates medical reports more accurately than SOTA models, outperforming them by 3 to 5 in several tasks. We find gains of 0.03 to 0.05 in METEOR and 0.02 to 0.05 in ROUGE scores, respectively, indicating improved recall and similarity in text-based assessments. In comparison to SOTA models, our models exhibit a 10 - 15% improvement in cross-modal alignment, according to the CMAI, and a 15 - 20% decrease in hallucination rates, according to the HRR. With a 0.03 - 0.07 rise in CCS values, the CCS further confirms that our models are more in line with clinical knowledge. The framework addresses model overconfidence, multi-modal integration, and hallucination reduction, advancing reliable AI-driven medical solutions. Code and data are available at: MLVLM.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Neural operators have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning solution operators of parametric PDEs, enabling rapid inference across parameter families without retraining. However, two critical challenges limit their effectiveness: inefficient multi-source feature fusion between data-domain (boundary condition) and physics-domain (PDE residual) representations, and pathological gradient imbalance caused by heterogeneous loss components during training. To address both challenges, we propose PIDANO (Physics-Informed Dual Adaptive Neural Operator), a general framework applicable to a broad class of parametric PDE problems. PIDANO introduces adaptive mechanisms into both the forward and backward passes of operator learning. The forward adaptive component synergizes adaptive activations, gated residual selection, and cross-attention fusion to precisely capture nonlinear data–physics interactions, replacing the static dot-product integration of standard DeepONets. The backward Operator Adaptive Balancing (OAB) leverages gradient statistics to dynamically rebalance heterogeneous loss contributions, resolving gradient conflicts between the PDE and boundary condition losses during training. All experiments are conducted under a purely unsupervised paradigm without any labeled interior data or paired simulation results. On three fluid dynamics benchmarks, PIDANO substantially outperforms PI-DeepONet, reducing mean relative error by 87.9%, 50.0%, and 39.4% on Kovasznay, Beltrami, and Lid-Driven Cavity Flows under out-of-distribution conditions, and by 59.6%, 86.4%, and 42.6% under in-distribution conditions.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Monitoring the safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) under extreme operating conditions faces significant challenges, due to the difficulty of conventional battery management systems (BMS) in capturing internal dynamic changes in real-time. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an implantable flexible sensor based on ZnO-passivated CsPbBr3 quantum dots encapsulated in EPDM, which realizes real-time monitoring inside lithium batteries. Experiments demonstrate that the sensor resistance exhibits high synchronization with battery voltage changes (response time < 5 s), and the capacity fade rate difference after sensor implantation is only 14.2 % over 15 days. Theoretical calculations and in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD) reveal the energy band modulation mechanism of Li+ adsorption-induced. During LIBs charging/discharging, changes in Li+ concentration around the sensor alter the band structure and density of states (DOS) of the sensing material, leading to changes in its electrical signal. Thus, the working state of the LIBs can be monitored and predicted by tracking changes in the sensor's electrical signal. Further integration of an LSTM-multitask learning model enables advanced prediction of the LIBs operating state based on sensor signals (5000 s ahead), with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 6.10 %, and charge/discharge rate recognition with 96.7 % accuracy.

abstract-evidence.abstract: Accurate in-situ thermal imaging of lithium-ion batteries is crucial for their safety, performance, and longevity. However, traditional methods struggle to generate physically consistent temperature maps from sparse sensor data. This study proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for in-situ two-dimensional temperature field imaging using distributed optical fiber sensing (DOFS) data. By introducing a Laplace-based spatial regularization prior into the training process, the proposed PINN model reconstructs smooth and physically consistent temperature fields from sparse fiber-path measurements and battery operating variables. The reconstructed temperature distributions are validated against infrared thermal images under multiple operating conditions. Across the tested conditions, the proposed PINN model achieved a average root mean square error of 0.2471 °C and a mean absolute percentage error of 0.5478%. Compared with linear and radial basis function (RBF) interpolation, the proposed PINN model achieves higher mean relative physical fidelity (RPF) across all state of charge levels and operating conditions, with average RPF scores of 85.05 for PINN, 77.50 for RBF, and 24.07 for linear interpolation. Additional tests under changed sensing layouts and ambient temperature conditions further support the applicability of the proposed framework for environment-aware temperature field reconstruction after condition-aware calibration. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately reconstructs physically consistent temperature fields from sparse DOFS data and supports in-situ thermal monitoring in battery systems.
